stories.title: Misiorowski Historic Start — 12 Ks, 7 Consecutive Strikeouts to Open
stories.angle: Jacob Misiorowski delivered one of the most dominant starts in Brewers history Sunday. He struck out the first 7 Colorado Rockies batters consecutively — a Brewers franchise record — and finished with 12 strikeouts in 5 innings in an 11-2 win. He threw 33 fastballs at 103+ mph, more than twice the previous single-game record since pitch tracking began. The only blemish: a solo HR by Cole Carrigg on a 102 mph fastball. His 9th game with 10+ strikeouts this season tied the Brewers single-season record (Corbin Burnes, 2022). Cy Young case just got stronger.

Misiorowski Historic Start vs Rockies
**Source:** Bleacher Report, CBS Sports, ESPN, Yahoo Sports, Brew Crew Ball (multiple confirmed)

- Misiorowski started Aug 23 vs Colorado Rockies — CONFIRMED

- 33 fastballs at 103+ mph — more than twice the previous single-game record since pitch tracking began — CONFIRMED (CBS Sports)

**Note on "Ben Sheets 2024" reference:** One source mentioned "Ben Sheets" in relation to the Brewers record. Ben Sheets pitched for Milwaukee in the early 2000s, not 2024. Research agent flagged this as a source error. The established record being broken is Corbin Burnes 2022 — using that.
**Note on "66 pitches over 100 MPH":** One YouTube headline cited 66 pitches at 100+ mph vs. CBS Sports' 33 pitches at 103+ mph. These thresholds are different (100 mph vs 103 mph) so not contradictory. Using the CBS Sports 103 mph figure as it is more precise and widely cited.

stories.title: Alvarez Triple Crown — 33 Games, One HR Back, Cabrera 2012 Context
stories.angle: Yordan Alvarez leads baseball in batting average (.329) and RBI (88) but trails Kyle Schwarber by one home run (37 vs 36). The Triple Crown math is still viable, but the window is narrowing. The last player to win a Triple Crown was Miguel Cabrera in 2012 — a fact worth restating to calibrate the historical weight of what Alvarez is pursuing. September arrives in 9 days. Every home run counts.

stories.title: Joshua Baez — Cardinals Rookie, One Week of Adjustments Later
stories.angle: Joshua Baez entered baseball history on August 15 with 3 HRs in his first 3 career at-bats (MLB first). One week into his professional career, he's at .251/.332/.552 with 12 home runs and a 32.7% strikeout rate. The chess match between Baez and MLB pitching staffs is now well underway. Baez has the power and athleticism to sustain — the question is whether he can cut the strikeout rate before pitchers fully map his approach.
